messages:
jess: Heads-up — getting multiple 504/timeouts on hosted /v1/generate (large requests). Seen from 08:12 UTC, p95 spike and customers reporting errors. starting a quick war room.
opsbot: Incident created: INC-3928475610 — tagging oncall and infra.
mike: I'm looking at ingress NLB and api-gateway logs now. any repro payloads?
jess: @mike yes — one example payload (an embeddings/batch job ~150k tokens) — customer says it used to work last week.
sarah: Checking gateway connection metrics — I see a flurry of TCP RESETs between apigw and runtime pool around the same time.
raj: grep'd the runtime logs — backend accepted the request but we see a client-side FIN mid-response. looks like connections being torn.
emily: customer payloads are huge and include long-ish streaming, might be keeping connections open longer than our default NLB idle timeout.
tim: NLB idle timeout is 350s? we recently lowered keepalive on the gateway pool to 60s in the connpool perf change (PR #1423). that could be the mismatch.
mike: confirm: apigw keepalive=60s, NLB idle=350s => mismatch usually tolerable, but if client stalls netlink might FIN earlier. but we see resets from the NLB side.
raj: tcpdump snippet from runtime node shows RST from target after server sends response headers, then large body in transfer:
```tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 10.4.5.6 and port 443```
jess: So hypothesis: connpool change (short keepalive) + large streaming/embedding requests => premature connection teardown + partial responses => 504/timeouts to client. agreed?
sarah: +1. also saw connection queue bursts saturating worker accept backlog for a few secs.
tim: immediate mitigations I can push: revert connpool keepalive to 300s on apigw (rollback of PR #1423) and increase NLB idle timeout to 900s for the cluster. also add a temporary request-size (token) guard on hosted endpoints to fail early with 413 instead of letting them hang.
emily: If we add the token guard, we should surface a clear client error and docs note.
mike: I'll open NLB change with infra, but this needs a deploy window due to edge churn.
raj: I can patch runtime to gracefully close slow streams instead of RST — small fix and patchable.
jess: Order of ops: 1) tim revert connpool keepalive now (oncall-approved), 2) mike request NLB idle increase, 3) raj runtime graceful-close patch, 4) emily prepare client-facing comms & token limits. assign owners?
tim: i'm on (connpool revert) — ETA 12m.
mike: starting NLB change request, ping infra channel — ETA 30m.
raj: will draft runtime patch, can ship a canary in 40m.
emily: drafting customer comms, will post draft in #support in 20m.
jess: monitoring — watch p50/p95 and 504 count on console; escalate if no improvement in 10m after revert.
opsbot: Update: connpool revert deployed by tim at 08:24 UTC.
jess: seeing fewer 504s for the first customer (checking).
mike: NLB request open: INCINFRA-867, asked infra for 900s idle timeout, they're reviewing.
raj: pushed canary runtime fix to eu-west-1; logs show graceful closes now, less RST.
emily: support note ready: short explainer + suggested payload limits and workaround for customers.
jess: ok team — good mitigation set. we'll follow up with a postmortem and action items. provisional action items: - rollback connpool change permanently or add safety guard (owner: tim) - increase NLB idle timeout for serving clusters (owner: mike/infra) - add request token quota/early-reject on hosted endpoints (owner: emily/product) - runtime: graceful-stream-close and better logging for TCP resets (owner: raj) - add observability alert when RSTs > 1% and long-transfer sessions > 60s (owner: sarah) - customer comms & docs update (owner: emily)
jess: I'll schedule a postmortem sync tomorrow 11:00 UTC and link timeline + logs. please paste any follow-ups here. :thumbsup:
